hints: Focus on what hot acidified dichromate does to different types of alcohol, primary, secondary and tertiary behave very differently.
Work out the empirical formula of the organic product by dividing each % by the atomic mass, C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, then dividing by the smallest value.
Once you know the product is a carboxylic acid with a certain number of carbons, ask which starting alcohol could be oxidised all the way to that acid.
walkthrough:
**Recall alcohol oxidation**

Remember, hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a strong oxidising agent. Primary alcohols oxidise in two stages to carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols stop at ketones, and tertiary alcohols do not react.

$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH}$$

**Find the formula of the product**

Convert the percentages to moles by dividing by $A_r$. This gives you the simplest ratio of atoms.

$$\text{C}: \frac{58.8}{12.0} = 4.90, \quad \text{H}: \frac{9.8}{1.0} = 9.80, \quad \text{O}: \frac{31.4}{16.0} = 1.96$$

**Simplify to the empirical formula**

Divide all three values by the smallest (1.96) to get the ratio.

$$\text{C}: \frac{4.90}{1.96} \approx 2.5, \quad \text{H}: \frac{9.80}{1.96} = 5.0, \quad \text{O}: \frac{1.96}{1.96} = 1.0$$
Multiply by 2 to get whole numbers: $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. This is the formula of a carboxylic acid.

**Link product back to alcohol U**

A $\text{C}_5$ carboxylic acid, pentanoic acid, must come from a $\text{C}_5$ primary alcohol oxidised under hot conditions. That points directly to pentan-1-ol.

options.A: 2-methylbutan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol. The carbon bearing the OH has no H atoms, so it cannot be oxidised by acidified dichromate and no organic product would form.
options.B: 3-methylbutan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol. It oxidises only to a ketone, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, which contains one O atom, not the two O atoms in $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$ found by analysis.
options.C: Pentan-1-ol is a primary alcohol with 5 carbons. With hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ it oxidises fully to pentanoic acid, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$, which has 58.8% C, 9.8% H and 31.4% O by mass.
options.D: Propan-1-ol is primary so it does give a carboxylic acid, but only a 3-carbon acid, propanoic acid $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$. Its percentage composition is different from the $\text{C}_5$ product analysed.
